newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: BP Colombia urges probe into alleged rights abuse.
newsitem.headline: BP Colombia urges probe into alleged rights abuse.

text.p: The Colombian unit of oil giant British Petroleum called on Friday for an official investigation into recent reports linking it to alleged human rights violations in Colombia.

BP's Colombian subsidiary, BP Exploration Company (Colombia) Ltd., called for the probe in an open letter to chief prosecutor Alfonso Valdivieso, saying it hoped that a thorough investigation would clear the company's name and free it from "public ridicule."

The letter signed by John Doust, executive director of BP's operations in Colombia, said company employees had already been ordered to cooperate fully with any investigation opened by Valdivieso and make any and all company files available upon his request.

Recent accounts in British newspapers have alleged that BP -- the single largest foreign investor in Colombia -- fostered or had a shadowy role in rights abuses and even political killings carried out by right-wing death squads or paramilitary groups since 1991 in eastern Casanare province, where it operates the huge Cusiana and Cupiagua oil fields.

The reports, which have been strongly denied by BP, were based at least partly on a study drafted by several government agencies last year, including the prosecutor-general's office and Colombia's human rights ombudsman.
The study, a company of which was obtained by Reuters last week, does not mention BP by name.
In a statement issued on Thursday, Colombia's foreign ministry said the recent allegations against BP "merit the government's fullest attention."
It added, however, that "in the absence of judicial investigations it is irresponsible to give credit" to allegations of human rights violations committed by BP.

In his letter to Valdivieso, Doust said BP was urging him to open a wide-ranging investigation of the company to see whether any of its employees had ever "covered up, promoted or supported the supposed violation of human rights."
